claims.head: The Senators will send their checkers at Celebrini
claims.call: The Senators’ L4 (Cousins, Amadio and Pinto) spends at least 57% of its 5-on-5 time against the Sharks’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Senators keep sending Pinto’s line (Cousins, Amadio and Pinto) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Travis Green has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Sharks’ first line is Smith, Celebrini and Chernyshov.

claims.gist: At home, Travis Green likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Sharks’ first line.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 7 games cover only 29% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the third-lowest in the league (a typical team: 45%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Darnell Nurse is day to day and missed their last game. He is a top-pair defenseman. Dmitry Orlov has taken his spot beside Michael Kesselring.
Jake Sanderson is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 7 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Thomas Chabot has taken his spot beside Artem Zub.
William Eklund is out 10-12 weeks and has missed the last 4 games.
Artem Zub returned in their last game after missing 4 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Artem Zub was added to the roster on Oct 16 and has played beside Thomas Chabot.
Jordan Spence has started killing penalties: on the ice for 39% of the team’s shorthanded time in 8 games, up from 4% last season.

OTT.head: The Senators should be in control
OTT.body: Even though Ottawa may be without Sanderson, the Senators have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. It’s on the Sharks to make it a game, and they can if they keep shots to a minimum.

SJS.head: A steep climb for the Sharks
SJS.body: Even though Ottawa may be without Sanderson, the Senators have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Sharks’ best hope is keeping shots to a minimum, plus a big night in goal.
